issues.description: Field Farm.animals: the problem statement (UML and implementation instructions) requires Farm.animals to be a List<Animal> and explicitly instructs to initialize it with an ArrayList in the no-argument constructor. The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) instead declares the field as 'private Queue<Animal> animals;' and initializes it with 'new LinkedList<>()', and its getter/setter use Queue<Animal>. This type mismatch (List/ArrayList vs Queue/LinkedList and corresponding accessor signatures) contradicts the exercise specification and can confuse students or cause tests that expect List/ArrayList signatures to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the problem specification: change the Farm.animals declaration and accessor signatures to use List<Animal> and initialize it with an ArrayList in the no-argument constructor (e.g., private List<Animal> animals; public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }). Update getAnimals()/setAnimals() to use List<Animal>. Alternatively, if using a Queue/LinkedList was intentional, update the problem statement and UML to explicitly require Queue and LinkedList and adjust the textual instructions and tests accordingly.
